scenario.summary: The LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise involved a malicious package release that deployed Python startup hooks (.pth files and sitecustomize.py) to achieve automatic execution. Once activated, the payload harvested a wide range of credentials from cloud providers, developer tools, and browsers, while maintaining a remote code loader to execute additional instructions from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

meta.rationale: Focus on developer workstations, CI/CD runners, and production gateway hosts identified by the software inventory scan.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using malicious Python startup hooks in a compromised package to execute a remote code loader and exfiltrate credentials from developer and production environments.

hunt.name: LiteLLM Remote Code Loading and Exfiltration
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the second-stage behavior of the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise. It focuses on the activation of the remote code loader and the exfiltration of encrypted credential archives. The hunt correlates the presence of the compromised software version with network telemetry from DNS lookups and the creation of transient staging artifacts or lock files on the file system.

nodes.label: Python DNS lookups to C2 infrastructure

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, COUNT(*) AS count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%python%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%pip%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname
config.description: Identify Python processes resolving the exfiltration domain or the loader configuration source.
config.expected_signal: Python or pip processes communicating with the domains named in the report. Silence means no such resolutions were logged within the window.
